mainTopic: The end of פרק מאימתי (different honors and rewards for different people), and the opening of פרק סדר תעניות: the fast-day ceremony, the prayer leader, and the extra fast-day ברכות
overview: This amud closes the first פרק of מסכת תענית and opens the second. First the גמרא finishes a teaching that kings honor the humble servant by standing and ministers by bowing. רבי זירא pushes back: the wording of the verse shows the ministers do both. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a matching idea: צדיקים are rewarded with light and ישרים with joy. After the הדרן, a new משנה describes a public fast day. The תיבה is brought to the city square, ashes are placed on it and on everyone's head, and an elder rebukes the people, teaching that real תשובה matters more than sackcloth and fasting. An experienced, poor elder with children leads the prayers and says 24 ברכות, the daily 18 plus six more. רבי יהודה swaps זכרונות and שופרות for passages about famine and drought. Each special ברכה ends with 'He Who answered' a figure from the past, from אברהם through דוד and שלמה. The amud ends as the משנה begins a story, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Kings stand and ministers bow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the verse from ישעיהו. It shows that kings honor the humble servant by standing, and ministers honor him by bowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: '…to the one despised of men, to the one hated by nations, to a servant of rulers: kings shall see and stand up.' So kings honor him by standing. Ministers honor him by bowing, as the same verse says: 'Ministers, and they shall bow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started just before this passage. Each group gives its own kind of honor: kings stand up and ministers bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching splits the verse into two parts. 'Kings shall see and arise' is matched to kings, so they stand. 'Ministers, and they shall bow' is matched to ministers, so they bow. The point is that each level of person gives a different kind of honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing up as a sign of respect

phrases.english: to the one despised of men, to the one abhorred of nations,
to a servant of rulers:
Kings shall see and arise.
And ministers give honor by bowing,
as it is written: 'Ministers, and they shall bow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching and verse that began earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings honor the humble servant by standing, and ministers honor him by bowing.

steps.title: The verse shows the ministers do both
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא (some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני) objects. He points to the word 'and' in the verse, which shows the ministers both stand and bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected, and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני. If the verse had said 'And ministers shall bow,' you would be right. But it says 'Ministers, and they shall bow.' So the ministers do both: they stand and they bow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the reading from step 1. He says the ministers don't only bow; they also stand up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depends on where the word 'and' (ו) sits. If the verse had said 'וְשָׂרִים יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ,' ministers would only bow. Since it says 'שָׂרִים וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ,' the 'and' adds bowing on top of the standing just mentioned, so they do both.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying ministers don't bow. He agrees they bow. He is adding that they also stand, just like the kings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this,
and some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani:
If it had been written 'And ministers shall bow,'
it would be as you said;
now that it is written 'Ministers, and they shall bow,'
they do this and that.
phrases.notes: He means the ministers both stand up and bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 1 read the verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ministers only bow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'and' sits before 'they shall bow,' not before 'ministers.' That shows bowing is added to the standing already mentioned, so ministers do both.

steps.title: צדיקים get light, ישרים get joy
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a matching idea: different people get different rewards. צדיקים get light and ישרים get joy, both learned from one verse in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I too say something like this. Not everyone gets light, and not everyone gets joy. צדיקים get light and ישרים get joy. צדיקים get light, as it says: 'Light is sown for the צדיק.' ישרים get joy, as it says: 'And joy for the upright in heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds his own teaching. Like the kings and ministers who each give a different honor, different good people each get a different reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the two halves of תהלים 97:11 as two separate rewards for two groups. Light goes to the צדיקים and joy goes to the ישרים. 'I too say' links his idea to the pattern of splitting a verse between two groups, as in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: The first פרק ends with a theme: not everyone receives every honor or reward. Each group gets what fits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הַכֹּל לְאוֹרָה, וְלֹא הַכֹּל לְשִׂמְחָה.
phrases.english: Not all are for light, and not all are for gladness.
The righteous are for light, and the upright are for gladness.
The righteous are for light, as it is written: 'Light is sown for the righteous.'
And the upright get gladness, as it is written: 'And gladness for the upright in heart.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a matching teaching that splits a verse between two groups, like step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are rewarded with light and ישרים with joy. Not every reward goes to everyone.

steps.title: Hadran: closing פרק מאימתי
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first פרק of מסכת תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק מאימתי.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first פרק, called מאימתי. Nothing new is argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is the traditional formula said when finishing a פרק. It shows our wish to come back and learn it again. The next line starts a brand-new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
'From when,' the name of the first פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'From when'
phrases.notes: פרקים are named by their opening words, so this is the name of the first פרק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that steps 1-3 ended.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק מאימתי of מסכת תענית is complete.

steps.title: The fast-day ceremony: ark and ashes
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes what is done on a public fast day. The תיבה is taken out to the city square, and ashes are placed on it, on the leaders' heads, and on everyone's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the order of the fast days? They take the תיבה out to the city's main square. They put burnt ashes on top of the תיבה, on the head of the נשיא, and on the head of the אב בית דין. Then each person puts ashes on his own head.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה describing the public fast-day ceremony. Everyone joins in the signs of mourning, starting with the תיבה and the leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the steps in order: first the תיבה is brought out, then ashes go on it, then on the two top leaders, then on everyone else. Moving everything into the open street and using ashes are public signs of mourning and humility.

keyTerms.meaning: The order (procedure) of the fast days
The ark that holds the ספר תורה
The head of the court, second to the נשיא

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה starts the second פרק. The גמרא that follows will explain each part of the ceremony and why it is done.

phrases.english: What is the order of fast days?

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַתֵּיבָה, לִרְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר,
phrases.english: They take the ark out to the city square,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹתְנִין אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה עַל גַּבֵּי הַתֵּיבָה,
phrases.english: and they place burnt ashes on top of the ark,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְרֹאשׁ הַנָּשִׂיא, וּבְרֹאשׁ אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: and on the head of the Nasi, and on the head of the Av Beit Din,
and each and every one places ashes on his own head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a public fast the תיבה is brought to the city square, and ashes are placed on it, on the נשיא, on the אב בית דין, and on every person.

steps.title: The elder speaks words of rebuke
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: after the ashes, the eldest among them rebukes the people. He reminds them that God responded to the people of נינוה because of their תשובה, not because of their sackcloth and fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The elder among them speaks words of rebuke: 'Our brothers! The verse about the people of נינוה does not say that God saw their sackcloth and their fasting. It says that God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way. And the נביאים say: Tear your hearts and not your garments.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing the fast day. An elder gives a short speech telling the people that the fast only works if they truly change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes from the previous step, and the fasting itself, are outward signs. The elder warns that these are not the main thing. He proves from the story of נינוה, and from a פסוק in the נביאים, that God responds to a changed heart and changed actions.

keyTerms.meaning: The elder among them, the most senior scholar present
Words of rebuke that move people to do תשובה
The people of נינוה from ספר יונה
Sackcloth, rough clothing worn in mourning
Here it means the books of the נביאים

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme for the whole fast day: the outward actions are only there to bring the people to real תשובה.

phrases.english: The elder among them
says before them words of rebuke:
Our brothers!
It is not said about the people of Nineveh
'And God saw their sackcloth and their fasting,'
rather: 'And God saw their deeds,
that they turned from their evil way,'
and in the Prophets it says:
phrases.notes: Here קבלה means the books of the נביאים.

phrases.english: 'Tear your hearts and not your garments.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזָּקֵן שֶׁבָּהֶן אוֹמֵר לִפְנֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי כִבּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order of the fast day after the ashes are placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An elder rebukes the people and reminds them that real תשובה, not outward signs of mourning, is what counts.

steps.title: Choosing the right prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: When they stand to pray, they choose a שליח ציבור who is old, experienced, has children, and is poor, so that he will pray with his whole heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: They stood for prayer. They send down before the ark an elder who is experienced, who has children, and whose house is empty, so that his heart will be fully in his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to the תפילה itself. It describes who should lead the prayers on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each quality is meant to make the prayer heartfelt. Someone with children to feed and nothing at home feels the community's need himself. So he will pray for rain and help with real feeling.

keyTerms.meaning: They send down before the ark, meaning they appoint him to lead the prayers
His house is empty, meaning he is poor
His heart is complete, fully focused

phrases.english: They stood for prayer —
they send down before the ark
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's way of saying they appoint him to lead the prayers.

phrases.english: an elder who is experienced
and who has children,
and whose house is empty,
so that his heart will be complete in prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rebuke to the prayer service that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שליח ציבור on a fast day should be an experienced elder with children who is poor, so he prays wholeheartedly.

steps.title: The twenty-four blessings of the fast day
steps.stepSummary: The שליח ציבור says 24 ברכות: the regular 18 plus six more. The six are זכרונות, שופרות, and four chapters of תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says twenty-four blessings before them: the eighteen of every day, and he adds six more. These are: זכרונות and שופרות, 'In my distress I called to ה׳ and He answered me,' 'I will lift up my eyes to the mountains,' 'Out of the depths I have called You, ה׳,' and 'A prayer of the afflicted when he faints.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us what the prayer leader says. He adds six special sections to the usual שמונה עשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual weekday עמידה has 18 ברכות. On a fast day, six are added, for 24 in total. The added sections are about crying out to ה׳ from trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighteen ברכות of the daily עמידה
Remembrances, the section of ראש השנה מוסף about ה׳ remembering
The section of ראש השנה מוסף with פסוקים about the שופר

steps.confusionAlert: The count is 24 only because the six extra sections are added on top of the regular 18. זכרונות and שופרות count as two of the six.

phrases.english: And he says before them
twenty-four blessings:
the eighteen of every day,
and he adds to them another six,
and these are: Remembrances and Shofarot,
'To the Lord in my distress I called, and He answered me,'
phrases.notes: This and the next three are openings of chapters in תהלים: 120, 121, 130, and 102.

phrases.english: 'I will lift up my eyes to the mountains, etc.,'
'Out of the depths I have called You, Lord,'
'A prayer of the afflicted when he faints.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After choosing the prayer leader, the משנה describes what he says.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a fast day the שליח ציבור says 24 ברכות: the daily 18 plus זכרונות, שופרות, and four chapters of תהלים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה replaces זכרונות and שופרות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. He holds that זכרונות and שופרות are not needed. In their place, the leader says two other passages about famine, plague, and drought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He did not need to say זכרונות and שופרות. Rather, he says instead of them: 'If there is famine in the land, if there is plague,' and 'The word of ה׳ that came to ירמיהו concerning the droughts.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different opinion about two of the six added sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees there are six added sections. He only swaps זכרונות and שופרות, which come from ראש השנה, for two passages that speak directly about famine and drought. Those passages fit the reason for the fast better.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא's six extra sections include זכרונות and שופרות. רבי יהודה replaces those two with passages about famine and drought.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He did not need to say
Remembrances and Shofarot,
rather, he says instead of them:

phrases.aramaic: ״רָעָב כִּי יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ דֶּבֶר כִּי יִהְיֶה״,
phrases.english: 'If there is famine in the land, if there is plague,'

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר הָיָה דְבַר ה׳ אֶל יִרְמְיָהוּ עַל דִּבְרֵי הַבַּצָּרוֹת״.
phrases.english: 'The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the droughts.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view on two of the six added sections listed in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the passages about famine and drought are said instead of זכרונות and שופרות.

steps.title: How the ברכות end: the first one, about אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The שליח ציבור says a special ending for each ברכה. The first one mentions how God answered אברהם on הר המוריה, and it closes with גואל ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also says their endings. For the first one he says: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Redeemer of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us how each special ברכה ends. It starts with the first ending, which recalls God answering אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ending reminds God of a time He answered someone in trouble, and asks Him to answer us the same way today. The first one closes with גואל ישראל. That is the same closing as one of the regular weekday ברכות, so this ברכה is a longer version of a regular one.

keyTerms.meaning: Their endings, meaning the closing lines of the ברכות
Mount Moriah, where the עקדה took place
Redeemer of Israel, a closing line also used in the weekday עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: There are seven endings, but only six extra ברכות were added in step 8. The 'first' one here is not one of the six extras. It is the regular weekday ברכה of גואל ישראל with a longer ending added.

phrases.english: And he says their endings.
For the first one he says:
He Who answered Avraham on Mount Moriah
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Redeemer of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of the 24 ברכות by giving the endings of the special ones
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each special ברכה ends with 'He Who answered…' followed by its own closing line. The first recalls אברהם and closes with גואל ישראל.

steps.title: The second ending: our ancestors at the sea
steps.stepSummary: The second ending recalls how God answered our ancestors at ים סוף, and it closes with זוכר הנשכחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the second one he says: 'He Who answered our ancestors at ים סוף will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who remembers forgotten things.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the second special ברכה, which recalls the splitting of the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the ברכה of זכרונות, the verses about God remembering. So its closing line fits that theme: God 'remembers what is forgotten.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Sea of Reeds, which split for בני ישראל

phrases.english: For the second one he says:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף
phrases.english: He Who answered our ancestors at the Sea of Reeds
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who remembers forgotten things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of endings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second ending recalls ים סוף and closes with זוכר הנשכחות.

steps.title: The third ending: יהושע at גלגל
steps.stepSummary: The third ending recalls how God answered יהושע at גלגל, and it closes with שומע תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the third one he says: 'He Who answered יהושע at גלגל will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears the תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the third special ברכה, which recalls יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the ברכה of שופרות, the verses about the שופר. So it closes with 'Who hears the תרועה,' which is the sound of the שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where יהושע and the people camped after entering the land
Who hears the תרועה, the שופר blast

phrases.english: For the third one he says:
He Who answered Yehoshua at Gilgal
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears the teruah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of endings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third ending recalls יהושע at Gilgal and closes with שומע תרועה.

steps.title: The fourth and fifth endings: שמואל and אליהו
steps.stepSummary: The fourth ending recalls שמואל at מצפה and closes with שומע צעקה. The fifth recalls אליהו on הר הכרמל and closes with שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the fourth one he says: 'He Who answered שמואל in מצפה will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears cries.' For the fifth one he says: 'He Who answered אליהו on הר הכרמל will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list with two more endings, one about שמואל and one about אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both use the same 'He Who answered' pattern. Only the person, the place, and the closing words change. Here the closings are about God hearing our cries and our prayers.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where שמואל gathered the people to pray
The mountain where אליהו faced the נביאי הבעל

phrases.english: For the fourth one he says:
He Who answered Shmuel in Mitzpah
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears cries.
For the fifth one he says:
He Who answered Eliyahu on Mount Carmel
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next items in the list of endings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth ending recalls שמואל and closes with שומע צעקה. The fifth recalls אליהו and closes with שומע תפלה.

steps.title: The sixth and seventh endings: יונה, then דוד and שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The sixth ending recalls יונה inside the fish and closes with העונה בעת צרה. The seventh recalls דוד and שלמה in ירושלים and closes with המרחם על הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the sixth one he says: 'He Who answered יונה from inside the fish will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who answers in a time of trouble.' For the seventh one he says: 'He Who answered דוד and his son שלמה in ירושלים will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who has mercy on the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the list of endings with the last two, about יונה and about דוד and שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes seven endings in all: the longer weekday ברכה plus the six extras. The final closing, 'Who has mercy on the land,' fits a fast day called because of trouble in the land, like a drought.

keyTerms.meaning: Who answers in a time of trouble
Who has mercy on the land

steps.whatToRemember: All seven endings follow one pattern: 'He Who answered [someone] will answer you.' The person and the closing line change each time. The first is the regular ברכה of גואל ישראל made longer. The other six are the extra fast-day ברכות.

phrases.english: For the sixth one he says:
He Who answered Yonah from inside the fish
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הָעוֹנֶה בְּעֵת צָרָה״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who answers in a time of trouble.
For the seventh one he says:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת דָּוִד וְאֶת שְׁלֹמֹה בְּנוֹ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: He Who answered David and his son Shlomo in Yerushalayim
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
